Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Candidate packaging checks

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

python3 -B tests/replay_dockyard/package/package_test.py uses opaque synthetic bytes to check exact copying, matching runtime-cohort binding, existing-output preservation, corruption detection and symlink refusal. It runs no Native engine, browser, compiler or network service and supplies no gameplay qualification.

Actual moved Native/Web candidate execution and original qualification records are separate evidence. The package manifest always declares release_admitted false; a copied runtime PASS cannot override a rejected qualification or missing public-network/human-review gates.

runtime.py --package ABS --out NEW --godot ABS copies the frozen candidate to a new location, removes source-root environment variables and runs a real Native Host/Client pair. It requires full state, terminal acknowledgement, one backend and typed cleanup. Only exact reload copies belonging to its actor PIDs are removed before verifying the original and moved package bytes again.

The CLI prints a manifest SHA256. package.py verify --package ABS --manifest-sha256 HEX pins that manifest as well as checking its payload map. The manifest is an integrity record; it does not establish release admission or sender authorization.

python3 -B tests/replay_dockyard/package/itch_test.py checks the itch ZIP's root entry point, runtime-byte preservation, license/QA inclusion, reproducible ZIP bytes, source/output integrity, and the explicit Butler upload option. Node runs the generated HTML bootstrap against nested URLs with existing query values and fragments. These synthetic checks do not qualify browser gameplay or itch hosting.

node tests/replay_dockyard/package/itch_smoke.mjs EXTRACTED_ZIP_DIRECTORY NEW_OUTPUT boots the actual packaged game in a separate Chrome profile at a nested URL with no launch query. It checks isolation, configured menu readiness, applied Room/TURN defaults and typed backend/full-engine exit. The saved screenshot and console report cover local startup only; hosted itch embedding and off-network multiplayer remain separate checks. This fixture uses the installed macOS Chrome executable.
